title: INT 67h, the EMS expanded memory services
covers: INT 67h, the LIM EMS expanded memory manager calls selected by AH.

rows.text: INT 67h AH=40h gets the status of the LIM EMS manager.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h.
The status can be 80h, 81h or 84h.
The call can be used only after establishing that the EMS driver is in fact present.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x40 of its switch on AH.
This case stores EMM_NO_ERROR in AH, where the document allows 80h, 81h or 84h.
INT 67h AH=41h gets the segment of the EMS page frame.
AH is the status.
AH 00h means the function was successful.
On success BX is the segment of the page frame.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x41 of its switch on AH.
INT 67h AH=42h gets the number of EMS pages.
AH is the status.
AH 00h means the function was successful.
On success BX is the number of unallocated pages.
On success DX is the total number of pages.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x42 of its switch on AH.
DX is the largest free memory block divided by 4 (MEM_FreeLargest()/4), capped at 0x7FFF, not a fixed total of pages.
The unallocated page count is also capped at 0x7FFF.
INT 67h AH=43h gets a handle and allocates memory.
BX is the number of logical pages to allocate.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, 85h, 88h or 89h.
The status can be 80h, 81h, 84h or 87h.
DX is the handle if AH is 00h.
The call allocates memory for a new handle.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x43 of its switch on AH.
The handle is the lowest free handle number from 1 up.
With dbg_zero_on_ems_allocmem set, EMS_ZeroAllocation writes a zero to every byte of the allocated memory.
The callee returns EMM_ZERO_PAGES, EMM_OUT_OF_LOG, EMM_OUT_OF_HANDLES and EMM_NO_ERROR, and the case stores that value in AH.
INT 67h AH=44h is the LIM EMS call that maps memory.
AL is the physical page number (0-3).
BX is the logical page number.
BX of FFFFh unmaps the page, which the list marks as QEMM.
DX is the handle.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, 83h, 8Ah or 8Bh.
The status can be 80h, 81h or 84h.
The call maps logical page BX of handle DX at physical page AL.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x44 of its switch on AH.
Before mapping or unmapping, the call turns the A20 gate on if it is off.
The callee returns EMM_ILL_PHYS, EMM_NO_ERROR, EMM_INVALID_HANDLE and EMM_LOG_OUT_RANGE, and the case stores that value in AH.
INT 67h AH=45h releases a handle and its memory.
DX is the EMM handle.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h or 83h.
The status can be 80h, 81h, 84h or 86h.
The call releases the handle and its memory.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x45 of its switch on AH.
A handle with a non-zero page count has its memory freed; handle 0 then keeps page count 0 and stays in use, any other handle is marked free.
The call also clears the handle's saved-page-map flag and its name.
The callee returns EMM_INVALID_HANDLE and EMM_NO_ERROR, and the case stores that value in AH.
INT 67h AH=46h gets the EMM version.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h.
The status can be 80h, 81h or 84h.
AL is the EMM version number if AH is 00h.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x46 of its switch on AH.
This case stores EMM_NO_ERROR in AH, where the document allows 80h, 81h or 84h.
INT 67h AH=47h saves the mapping context.
DX is the handle.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, 83h or 8Dh.
The status can be 80h, 81h, 84h, 8Ch or 8Eh.
The call saves the mapping context.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x47 of its switch on AH.
Handle 0 is accepted whether or not it is allocated.
The callee returns EMM_INVALID_HANDLE, EMM_PAGE_MAP_SAVED and EMM_NO_ERROR, and the case stores that value in AH.
The call sets the handle's saved-page-map flag after copying the map, and a save for a handle whose flag is set returns EMM_PAGE_MAP_SAVED.
INT 67h AH=48h restores the mapping context.
DX is the handle.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, 83h or 8Eh.
The status can be 80h, 81h or 84h.
The call restores the mapping context.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x48 of its switch on AH.
Handle 0 is accepted whether or not it is allocated.
The callee returns EMM_INVALID_HANDLE, EMM_NO_SAVED_PAGE_MAP and the return of EMM_RestoreMappingTable, and the case stores that value in AH.
The call clears the handle's saved-page-map flag before restoring, and a restore of a handle whose flag is clear returns EMM_NO_SAVED_PAGE_MAP.
INT 67h AH=4Bh gets the number of EMM handles.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h.
The status can be 80h, 81h, 83h or 84h.
BX is the number of EMM handles if AH is 00h.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x4b of its switch on AH.
This case stores EMM_NO_ERROR in AH, where the document allows 80h, 81h, 83h or 84h.
INT 67h AH=4Ch gets the pages owned by a handle.
DX is the EMM handle.
AH is the status of the call.
BX is the number of logical pages if AH is 00h.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x4c of its switch on AH.
An invalid handle stores EMM_INVALID_HANDLE in AH.
A handle is valid when it is below EMM_MAX_HANDLES and its page count is not NULL_HANDLE.
A loop sets each handle's page count to NULL_HANDLE, and EMM_AllocateSystemHandle sets the OS handle's page count to the count it is given.
INT 67h AH=4Dh gets the pages for all handles.
ES:DI points to the array that receives the information.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h.
The status can be 80h, 81h or 84h.
If AH is 00h, BX is the number of active EMM handles.
The array is filled with 2-word entries, each a handle and the number of pages allocated to it.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x4d of its switch on AH.
The callee returns EMM_NO_ERROR, where the document allows 80h, 81h or 84h.
INT 67h AH=4Eh gets or sets the page map.
AL is the subfunction.
The function was designed to be used by multitasking operating systems and should not ordinarily be used by application software.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 8Fh.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x4e, which switches on AL.
INT 67h AH=4Eh AL=00h gets the mapping registers.
ES:DI points to the array that receives the information, for AL=00h or 02h.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, which means successful.
The status can be 80h, 81h, 84h, 8Fh or A3h.
The array pointed to by ES:DI receives the mapping information, for AL=00h or 02h.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x4e, then by case 0x00 of its switch on AL.
This case stores EMM_NO_ERROR in AH, where the document allows 80h, 81h, 84h, 8Fh or A3h.
INT 67h AH=4Eh AL=01h sets the mapping registers.
DS:SI points to the array holding the information, for AL=01h or 02h.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, which means successful.
The status can be 80h, 81h, 84h, 8Fh or A3h.
The call sets the mapping registers from the array.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x4e, then by case 0x01 of its switch on AL.
The case stores the return of EMM_RestoreMappingTable, which returns EMM_NO_ERROR.
INT 67h AH=4Eh AL=02h gets and sets the mapping registers at once.
DS:SI points to the array holding the information, for AL=01h or 02h.
ES:DI points to the array that receives the information, for AL=00h or 02h.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, which means successful.
The status can be 80h, 81h, 84h, 8Fh or A3h.
The array pointed to by ES:DI receives the mapping information, for AL=00h or 02h.
The call sets the mapping registers from the array at DS:SI.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x4e, then by case 0x02 of its switch on AL.
The case stores the return of EMM_RestoreMappingTable, which is EMM_NO_ERROR.
INT 67h AH=4Eh AL=03h gets the size of the page-mapping array.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, which means successful.
The status can be 80h, 81h, 84h, 8Fh or A3h.
AL is the number of bytes in the page-mapping array, for AL=03h only.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x4e, then by case 0x03 of its switch on AL.
This case stores EMM_NO_ERROR in AH, where the document allows 80h, 81h, 84h, 8Fh or A3h.
INT 67h AH=4Fh gets or sets a partial page map.
AL is the subfunction.
AL=00h gets the partial page map.
For AL=00h, DS:SI points to a structure containing the list of segments whose mapping contexts are to be saved.
For AL=00h, ES:DI points to the array to receive the page map.
AL=01h sets the partial page map.
For AL=01h, DS:SI points to the structure containing the saved partial page map.
AL=02h gets the size of the partial page map.
For AL=02h, BX is the number of mappable segments in the partial map to be saved.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, 84h or 8Bh.
The status can be 8Fh.
The status can be 80h or 81h.
8Bh means one of the specified segments is not mappable.
A3h means the contents of the partial page map are corrupted or the count of mappable segments exceeds the total number of mappable segments in the system.
AL is the size of the partial page map for subfunction 02h.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x4f of its switch on AH.
An AL other than 00h, 01h or 02h logs an error and returns EMM_FUNC_NOSUP, defined as 0x84, where the document says 8Fh, which the source defines as EMM_INVALID_SUB.
The function returns EMM_ILL_PHYS, EMM_RestoreMappingTable's return, EMM_FUNC_NOSUP and EMM_NO_ERROR, at the lines cited.
The function itself returns no A3h: the count read from guest memory only bounds each loop and is never compared with the total of mappable segments.
INT 67h AH=50h maps or unmaps multiple handle pages.
AL is the subfunction.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h.
The status can be 8Fh.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x50, which stores EMM_NO_ERROR in AH and then switches on AL.
INT 67h AH=50h AL=00h maps or unmaps multiple pages using physical page numbers.
DX is the handle.
CX is the number of entries in the array.
DS:SI points to the mapping array.
Each array entry is a word logical page number, then a word physical page number.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, 83h, 8Ah or 8Bh.
The status can be 80h, 81h or 84h.
A logical page number of FFFFh unmaps the physical page.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x50, then by case 0x00 of its switch on AL.
This case stores AH only with the return of EMM_MapPage and has no store of 0x80, 0x81 or 0x84 of its own.
INT 67h AH=50h AL=01h maps or unmaps multiple pages using segment addresses.
DX is the handle.
CX is the number of entries in the array.
DS:SI points to the mapping array.
Each array entry is a word logical page number, then a word segment address.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, 83h, 8Ah or 8Bh.
The status can be 80h, 81h or 84h.
A logical page number of FFFFh unmaps the page at the segment.
Any other logical page number is mapped from the handle at the segment.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x50, then by case 0x01 of its switch on AL.
Segments are accepted by the machine type: EMS_MIXED and EMS_EMM386 take any segment below 0x10000, other types only 0xA000-0xAFFF and the EMS page frame.
When the computed physical page number is outside 0 to EMM_MAX_PHYS-1, the segment is recorded in emm_segmentmappings at segment>>10 instead of emm_mappings, both when unmapping and when mapping.
The callee returns EMM_NO_ERROR, EMM_INVALID_HANDLE, EMM_LOG_OUT_RANGE and EMM_ILL_PHYS, at the lines cited.
INT 67h AH=51h reallocates pages.
DX is the handle.
BX is the number of pages to be allocated to the handle.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, 83h or 88h.
The status can be 80h, 81h, 84h or 87h.
BX is the actual number of pages allocated to the handle.
The call reallocates the pages of the handle.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x51 of its switch on AH.
The case passes reg_bx to EMM_ReallocatePages as a const reference and stores only reg_ah, so BX keeps the requested count.
The callee returns EMM_INVALID_HANDLE, EMM_OUT_OF_LOG and EMM_NO_ERROR, at the lines cited.
INT 67h AH=52h gets or sets handle attributes.
AL is the subfunction.
AL=00h gets the handle attributes.
For AL=00h, AL is the attribute: 00h handle is volatile, 01h handle is nonvolatile.
AL=01h sets the handle attributes.
For AL=01h, BL is the new attribute: 00h handle is volatile, 01h handle is nonvolatile.
AL=02h gets the attribute capability.
For AL=02h, AL is the attribute capability: 00h only volatile handles supported, 01h both volatile and non-volatile.
DX is the handle.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, 83h, 8Fh, 90h or 91h.
The status can be 80h, 81h or 84h.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x52 of its switch on AH.
For a valid handle, AL=00h stores EMM_VOLATILE in AL and no other value, so a nonvolatile handle is never reported.
A BL of EMM_VOLATILE is accepted and stored nowhere, and the case then runs on into the code of AL=02h, which stores EMM_VOLATILE in AL.
EMM_NONVOLATILE returns EMM_FEAT_NOSUP and any BL other than EMM_VOLATILE or EMM_NONVOLATILE returns EMM_ATTR_UNDEF.
The function returns EMM_INVALID_HANDLE, EMM_FEAT_NOSUP, EMM_ATTR_UNDEF, EMM_INVALID_SUB and EMM_NO_ERROR, at the lines cited.
INT 67h AH=53h gets or sets the handle name.
AL is the subfunction.
AL=00h gets the handle name.
For AL=00h, ES:DI points to the 8-byte buffer for the handle name.
AL=01h sets the handle name.
For AL=01h, DS:SI points to the 8-byte handle name.
DX is the handle.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, 83h or 8Fh.
The status can be 80h, 81h, 84h or A1h.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x53 of its switch on AH.
The function returns EMM_INVALID_HANDLE, EMM_INVALID_SUB and EMM_NO_ERROR, at the lines cited.
INT 67h AH=54h gets the handle directory.
AL is the subfunction.
AL=00h gets the handle directory.
For AL=00h, ES:DI points to the buffer for the handle directory.
AL=01h searches for a named handle.
For AL=01h, DS:SI points to the 8-byte name.
AL=02h gets the total number of handles.
For subfunction 00h, AL is the number of entries in the handle directory.
For subfunction 01h, DX is the value of the named handle.
For subfunction 02h, BX is the total number of handles.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, 8Fh or A0h.
The status can be 80h, 81h or 84h.
A1h means a handle found had no name.
A directory entry begins with the handle as a word.
The handle's 8-byte name follows the handle in a directory entry.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x54 of its switch on AH.
The function returns EMM_NO_ERROR, EMM_NOT_FOUND and EMM_INVALID_SUB, at the lines cited.
The search returns the first handle whose stored name equals the 8 bytes, even an empty name, and EMM_NOT_FOUND when none does.
INT 67h AH=58h gets the mappable physical address array.
AL is the subfunction.
AL=00h gets the mappable physical address array.
For AL=00h, ES:DI points to the buffer to be filled with the array.
AL=01h gets the number of entries in the array.
CX is the number of entries in the array.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h.
The status can be 80h, 81h, 84h or 8Fh.
The returned array for subfunction 00h is filled in physical segment address order.
An array entry begins with the physical page segment as a word.
The physical page number follows the segment in an array entry, as a word.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x58 of its switch on AH.
An AL other than 00h also gets the count in CX and the status EMM_NO_ERROR, with no array written.
For every AL the case ends by storing EMM_NO_ERROR in AH, so an undefined AL gets 00h and not 8Fh.
INT 67h AH=57h moves or exchanges a memory region.
AL is the subfunction.
AL=00h moves the memory region.
AL=01h exchanges the memory region.
DS:SI points to the structure describing the source and the destination.
AH is the status of the call.
The source and destination may overlap for a move, and the copy direction is chosen such that the destination receives an intact copy of the source region.
The structure begins with the region length in bytes, as a dword.
At offset 04h a byte gives the source memory type: 00h conventional, 01h expanded.
At offset 05h a word gives the source handle.
The source handle is 0000h if the memory is conventional.
At offset 07h a word gives the source initial offset: within the page if EMS, and as the list words it, segment if conventional.
At offset 09h a word gives the source initial segment for conventional memory or the logical page for EMS.
At offset 0Bh a byte gives the destination memory type: 00h conventional, 01h expanded.
At offset 0Ch a word gives the destination handle.
At offset 0Eh a word gives the destination initial offset.
At offset 10h a word gives the destination initial segment or page.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x57 of its switch on AH.
The loop copies from the start of the region upward in blocks of at most MEM_PAGE_SIZE bytes, advancing both pointers after each block.
For conventional memory the offset word is added to the segment word times 16 (912, 923); for expanded memory it is the offset within the page (919, 930).
The A20 gate is turned on for the copy and put back to its earlier state afterwards.
The call logs an error when the status is not 0.
INT 67h AH=59h gets expanded memory hardware information.
AL is the subfunction.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be A4h, access denied by the operating system.
Subfunction 00h is for use by operating systems only, and can be enabled or disabled at any time by the operating system.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x59, which stores EMM_NO_ERROR in AH and then switches on AL.
The case stores EMM_NO_ERROR in AH before the switch, and the default branch stores EMM_INVALID_SUB for another AL, where the document allows A4h.
INT 67h AH=59h AL=00h gets the hardware configuration array.
ES:DI points to the buffer to be filled with the array.
The call fills the buffer at ES:DI with the hardware configuration array.
The word at offset 00h of the array is the size of raw EMM pages in paragraphs.
The word at offset 02h of the array is the number of alternate register sets.
The word at offset 04h of the array is the size of the mapping-context save area in bytes.
The word at offset 06h of the array is the number of register sets assignable to DMA.
The word at offset 08h of the array is the DMA operation type: 0000h is DMA with alternate register sets, 0001h is only one DMA register set.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x59, then by case 0x00 of its switch on AL.
INT 67h AH=59h AL=01h gets the unallocated raw page count.
BX is the number of unallocated raw pages.
DX is the total number of raw pages.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x59, then by case 0x01 of its switch on AL.
DX is stored as MEM_TotalPages()/4, and a comment on that line calls it not entirely correct.
INT 67h AH=5Ah allocates standard or raw pages.
AL is the subfunction.
AL=00h allocates standard pages.
AL=01h allocates raw pages.
BX is the number of pages to allocate.
DX is the handle.
AH is the status of the call.
The status can be 00h, 85h or 88h.
The status can be 8Fh.
The status can be 80h, 81h, 84h or 87h.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x5a of its switch on AH.
AL=01h takes the same call as AL=00h, with the same arguments.
The call passes can_allocate_zpages as true, and the callee returns EMM_ZERO_PAGES only when it is false.
The case stores the callee's return, or EMM_INVALID_SUB for an AL above 01h, where the document allows 80h, 81h, 84h or 87h.

searched.gave: Not applicable: DOSBox-X has no MAME header, and its case 0x70 cites only a master.lib manual of a third party in a comment.
Nothing found: a web search for NEC PC-98 EMS INT 67h AH=70h returned only generic LIM EMS pages, no NEC document.
Not searched beyond the web search; no page naming INT 67h AH=70h turned up.
Not searched beyond the web search; no page naming INT 67h AH=70h turned up.
Ralf Brown's list has no INT 67 AH=70h section: its INT 67 headings run from AH=40h to AH=5Dh and from AH=69h to AH=6Bh, then AH=DDh.

rows.text: The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0x70 of its switch on AH.
The case tests AL against 1, and each of its branches stores EMM_INVALID_SUB in AH.
On PC-98 with AL=1, a BX of 0 or 1 logs that remapping the B000h page frame is not implemented; a larger BX logs that it will likely do nothing.
Outside PC-98 with AL=1, the case logs that the subfunction is not supported and stores EMM_INVALID_SUB in AH.
An AL other than 1 logs an error and stores EMM_INVALID_SUB in AH.
The INT 67h handler reaches it by case 0xDE of its switch on AH.
When VCPI is disabled, the case answers EMM_FUNC_NOSUP and logs the refusal.
The subfunction is selected by a second switch on AL.
A subfunction with no case of its own is answered with EMM_FUNC_NOSUP after a log line.
A refusal stores EMM_FUNC_NOSUP in AH.
VCPI setup stores the two PIC bases, and the EMS setup stores the protected mode entry point.

searched.gave: Not applicable: MAME does not model INT 67h, and the DOSBox-X case names no document.
Nothing found: a web search for the VCPI specification returned no document hosted by Phar Lap or Quarterdeck.
Nothing found: the same search returned no bitsavers page of a VCPI specification.
Nothing found: the same search returned no archive.org copy of a VCPI specification.
Ralf Brown's list documents each DEh subfunction in its own section and has none for the group.

rows.text: The installation check tells whether VCPI is present.
AH is the status of the call.
On success, BH is the major version number.
On success, BL is the minor version number.
The status is 00h when VCPI is present and nonzero when it is not.
The handler reaches it by case 0xDE of its switch on AH, then case 0x00 of its switch on AL.
The check answers present when CX is 0000h and DI is 0012h, or when the CPU is already in virtual 86 mode.
The call gets the protected mode interface of the VCPI server.
ES:DI points to the 4K page table buffer.
DS:SI points to three descriptor table entries in the GDT: the first becomes the code segment descriptor and the other two are for the main control program.
AH is 00h on success and nonzero on failure.
On success, DI points to the first unused page table entry in the buffer.
On success, EBX is the protected mode entry point.
The protected mode entry point may be called with AX=DE00h through DE05h and AX=DE0Ch.
The handler reaches it by case 0xDE of its switch on AH, then case 0x01 of its switch on AL.
With no client page directory, the case writes an identity page table for the first megabyte except its last 4K page, which entry FFh maps to page 110h.
The case points the page frame's four entries at the EMS pages mapped there.
The case writes three descriptor table entries at DS:SI: the callback segment as a code segment, then two full-access segments.
The entry point returned is the VCPI callback that the EMS setup installs.
The call gets the highest physical memory address.
AH is 00h on success and nonzero on failure.
On success, EDX is the physical address of the highest 4K memory page.
The handler reaches it by case 0xDE of its switch on AH, then case 0x02 of its switch on AL.
The call gets the number of free 4K pages.
AH is 00h on success and nonzero on failure.
On success, EDX is the number of free 4K pages.
The count covers the pages available to all tasks in the system.
The function is also available in protected mode through the protected mode entry point.
The handler reaches it by case 0xDE of its switch on AH, then case 0x03 of its switch on AL.
The call allocates a 4K page.
AH is 00h on success and nonzero on failure.
On success, EDX is the physical address of the allocated page.
The client program is responsible for freeing all memory allocated with this call before terminating.
The function is also available in protected mode through the protected mode entry point.
The handler reaches it by case 0xDE of its switch on AH, then case 0x04 of its switch on AL.
When no page can be allocated, the case stores EMM_OUT_OF_LOG in AH.
The call frees a 4K page.
EDX is the physical address of the 4K page.
AH is 00h on success and nonzero on failure.
The function is also available in protected mode through the protected mode entry point.
The handler reaches it by case 0xDE of its switch on AH, then case 0x05 of its switch on AL.
The call gets the physical address of a page in the first megabyte.
CX is the page number, the linear address shifted right 12 bits.
AH is the status: 00h on success and nonzero for an invalid page number.
On success, EDX is the physical address of the page.
The list recommends 8Bh for an invalid page number.
The handler reaches it by case 0xDE of its switch on AH, then case 0x06 of its switch on AL.
Inside the page frame, the case picks the mapped page by the quarter of the frame that CX addresses.
When that quarter holds no mapped page, the case stores EMM_ILL_PHYS in AH.
Outside the page frame, the case returns CX shifted left 12 bits, with no test of the page.
The call reads control register 0.
AH is 00h.
EBX is the value of control register 0.
The handler reaches it by case 0xDE of its switch on AH, then case 0x07 of its switch on AL.
The call gets the 8259 interrupt vector mappings.
AH is 00h on success and nonzero on failure.
On success, BX is the first vector used by the master 8259 (IRQ0).
On success, CX is the first vector used by the slave 8259 (IRQ8).
CX is undefined in systems without a slave 8259.
The handler reaches it by case 0xDE of its switch on AH, then case 0x0A of its switch on AL.
VCPI setup stores 08h as the master PIC base and 70h as the slave PIC base.
The call sets the 8259 interrupt vector mappings.
BX is the first vector used by the master 8259.
CX is the first vector used by the slave 8259.
The call is made with interrupts disabled.
AH is 00h on success and nonzero on failure.
The call only informs the server of a client's change; a client may not change mappings the server or another client changed, and must restore the originals before terminating.
The handler reaches it by case 0xDE of its switch on AH, then case 0x0B of its switch on AL.
The case clears the interrupt flag itself before storing the mappings.
VCPI setup stores 08h as the master PIC base and 70h as the slave PIC base.
The call switches from virtual 86 mode to protected mode.
ESI is the linear address in the first megabyte of the values for the system registers.
The call is made with interrupts disabled.
The call returns with interrupts disabled.
The call loads GDTR, IDTR, LDTR and TR.
SS:ESP must have at least 16 bytes of space, and the entry point is required to set up a new stack before enabling interrupts.
The call destroys DS, ES, FS and GS.
The call destroys EAX and ESI.
Calling the protected mode entry point with AX=DE0Ch and the registers and stack the note lists switches to virtual 86 mode.
The block at ESI holds CR3 at 00h, linear addresses of the GDTR and IDTR values at 04h and 08h, LDTR at 0Ch, TR at 0Eh and CS:EIP at 10h.
The handler reaches it by case 0xDE of its switch on AH, then case 0x0C of its switch on AL.
The case clears the interrupt flag itself before loading the tables.
The case frees the task state segment's busy bit in the GDT before loading TR.
Before the jump, the case clears the VM and NT flags and sets bits 12 and 13 of the flags.
The case jumps to the protected mode entry point instead of returning to the caller.
The case writes neither EAX nor ESI.
